sources.use: Comparison of the previous standard Human mechanics

blocks.text: In D&D 5.5e, Humans are adaptable Humanoids who choose Medium or Small size, walk 30 feet, gain Heroic Inspiration at the end of every Long Rest, select a skill proficiency, and gain an Origin feat of their choice. Resourceful, Skillful and Versatile make the revised Human flexible without tying that flexibility to increases in all six ability scores.

A Human's background now determines their starting ability-score adjustments and normally provides a separate Origin feat. Languages also come from the shared character-creation rules, not from a Human-only language trait. This entry uses the updated 2024 rules as described in official sources and SRD 5.2.1. No 2014 standard or Variant Human mechanics have been added to the new species package.

blocks.text: Keep the species choices separate in a character builder: choose size, one skill, and one Origin feat for Human; then apply the background's ability adjustments, assigned Origin feat and other benefits under the background rules. Starting languages are selected in the ordinary character-creation step.

Resourceful grants Heroic Inspiration when the Human finishes a Long Rest. Heroic Inspiration is a resource that can be spent immediately after rolling a die to reroll that die; the second result replaces the first even if it is worse. The resource can apply beyond d20 checks, but any individual reroll still follows the relevant game's timing and dice rules. In an Advantage or Disadvantage roll, only one d20 may be rerolled.

You cannot hold more than one instance of Heroic Inspiration. If you receive another while you already have one, you can pass that new instance to a player character in your group who lacks it. The Long Rest therefore guarantees a new opportunity to gain Inspiration, not an endlessly accumulating reserve. Resourceful does not itself create an additional reroll after every die roll.

Skillful provides proficiency in one skill of your choice. This is a flexible species choice, distinct from the skills supplied by your class and background. A trained investigator might choose Investigation, while a scout could choose Perception or Stealth; the best selection depends on what is already covered by the character's other options.

Versatile grants a chosen Origin feat in addition to the one normally specified by a background. The choice must be an Origin feat and must follow any eligibility requirements and feat rules, including limits on taking the same feat twice. Skilled is recommended in the official Human entry, but it is not mandatory. For example, Skilled can broaden skill and tool training, while Alert can support readiness in initiative.

blocks.title: Where scores and languages come from
blocks.text: The updated Human has no +1-to-every-score trait and no extra species language. Backgrounds normally provide ability adjustments and a specified Origin feat. The ordinary 2024 character-creation procedure grants Common plus two Standard Languages table choices; these are not a bonus from being Human.

The revised Human is a distinct 5.5e species entry, not a new instance of 2014 Variant Human. In the 2014 standard Human rules, all six ability scores increased by 1, Medium was the size and the species granted Common plus one extra language. The separate optional 2014 Variant Human instead used two chosen +1 ability increases, a chosen skill proficiency and a feat.

The 2024 Human no longer uses either of those ability-score packages. It gains Resourceful, Skillful and Versatile, can be Small or Medium, and uses the new background and language creation steps. A similar opportunity to start with a feat does not mean the two editions' feat rules or selectable packages are interchangeable.

blocks.title: Do not combine editions
blocks.text: Choose the full rules package for the edition in use. The species options are not independent enhancements that can be stacked onto a character without an explicit separate rule.

Human characters can come from many kinds of communities, including trading ports, remote farming settlements, mixed-species cities, nomadic communities and centers of scholarship. Adaptability can be reflected through practical skills, shifting alliances and diverse ways of living rather than a single universal cultural identity.

The official multiverse includes some specific stories about Human origins, but those accounts do not establish that every fantasy setting has the same history. A campaign could feature Humans as recent newcomers, old inhabitants, traveling merchants or people with widely differing relationships to other species.

A Human's outlook should be built from family, training, work, language and personal choices. The revised rules offer flexible mechanics for portraying a wide range of personalities without assuming that all Humans are ambitious, heroic, diplomatic or alike.

Choose size to fit the character concept and expected play style; the 30-foot walking speed remains the same. Consider how the campaign's size-related movement and positioning rules affect the character, rather than assuming Small grants extra stealth or an automatic attack benefit. See [[rule:movement|Movement]] for the general mechanics.

Plan the skill choice after you know the class and background proficiencies. A [[class:fighter@5.5e|Fighter]] might use Skillful to improve out-of-combat investigation or awareness, while a [[class:wizard@5.5e|Wizard]] could expand social or exploration competence. Choose a skill that creates new opportunities rather than assuming that a duplicate proficiency doubles the proficiency bonus.

Use Versatile to choose an Origin feat that complements the character without relying on a feat of the wrong category. A Human looking for broad training might choose Skilled, if eligible; a character who wants to improve initiative support may choose Alert. The Human feat comes in addition to the background's specified Origin feat, so check both choices and any repeatability rules.

Plan Resourceful as a recurring opportunity for a reroll, not a guarantee of success. Consider spending Heroic Inspiration after a high-stakes die result, remembering that the new result must be kept. If an upcoming Long Rest would grant another instance while you still have one, the rules allow you to pass the new one to a teammate who lacks it.

items: Choose Medium or Small and record 30-foot walking speed.
Select the character's background and apply its allowed ability increases and Origin feat.
Add Skillful's one chosen skill proficiency and Versatile's additional eligible Origin feat.
Choose Common plus two standard languages using the general character-creation rules.
Track Heroic Inspiration and its Long Rest grant separately from other class or feat resources.
